newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Dalai Lama says Taiwan visit helps ties with China.
newsitem.headline: Dalai Lama says Taiwan visit helps ties with China.

text.p: Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, said on Monday he hoped his visit to Taiwan could reduce distance between Tibet and China, denying that he sought Tibet's independence or disliked the Chinese.

"I always consider that a close understanding between Tibet and the Chinese is extremely important," the Dalai Lama said in his first news conference since beginning his unprecedented visit to Nationalist-ruled Taiwan on Saturday.
"This visit can be very helpful to remove the feeling of distance between one another," he said.

The Dalai Lama, regarded by Tibetan Buddhists as a god-king, said he had never sought independence for his Himalayan homeland, though he noted Tibet had existed as an independent country. Nor did he dislike the Chinese, he said.

The Dalai Lama said he understood the vitriolic attacks on his Taiwan visit issued by communist China, which has assailed his expected meeting with Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui as the collusion of "splittists" bent on independence from China for Tibet and Taiwan.
"Although I can understand the negative response (from China), unfortunately all of my movements are considered splittist," he said.
"I don't want this visit to be politicised. If it is too politicised it benefits neither me nor you," he said.
